main_body: A flat ground patch of dark olive-green mossy grass, 4x3 tiles, with a repeating tile pattern of light and dark green speckle clumps and a few orange and brown dots.
top_band: none (terrain ground patch, no standing object)
evidence: The candidate is a flat terrain ground texture with no standing volume, so the top/front contract does not apply. There is no side face and no elevation drawing, and it is a seamless ground patch matching the terrain kind. Nothing here fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 5 green steps, from dark olive to light yellow-green, in clumps and speckles, so the shading is comparable to the grass reference. The texture is a tiled noise pattern that repeats exactly every 16px (each tile is identical, with the same orange and brown dots at the same positions), which looks mechanical next to the Beodeul grass. The orange dots are evenly spaced and read as artifacts rather than natural detail. There are no flat fills of 5x5 or more and no outlines. The density per tile is decent, but the strict repetition and the regular grid of dots make it look thinner and less natural than the reference. The patch also looks muddy and low in contrast, with horizontal banding in the dark areas. Strict call: fail.
